answer: Named: scarce-seed orchard mapping. Each identity must plant a unique walnut-sized seed in a shared orchard ledger, derived from a live entropy beacon at its zenith window; the seed's coordinates are non-reusable and expire after one epoch. Re-registering requires solving a fresh beacon-derived placement puzzle averaging 40 CPU-hours, and duplicate coordinate collisions void both entries. An attacker farming N sybils pays N×40 CPU-hours plus forfeiture of any collided seeds, making mass identity creation linear in compute rather than cheap.
